name: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve
blurb: Hardwood and hemlock forest on a deep river gorge, from beech nuts to bears.

tip.title: Remove the coyotes
tip.text: Coyotes are the main wild predator of fawns and small mammals here. Set Coyote to -100% and watch deer and rabbits, then the beech and wildflowers they eat.

sources.title: Wikipedia: New River Gorge National Park and Preserve

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (New River Gorge National Park and Preserve, American black bear, White-tailed deer). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A hardwood whose nuts (beechnuts) are eaten by black bears, squirrels and other forest animals.
A shade-tolerant conifer of moist ravines and hillsides, part of the hemlock-hardwood forest. Introduced woolly adelgids threaten it.
A dominant evergreen understory shrub of moist Appalachian slopes and streamsides that forms dense thickets and gives shelter to wildlife.

nodes.name: Orange jewelweed
nodes.desc: A moisture-loving wildflower of seeps and streambanks; GloBI records groundhogs and cottontails eating it.
The park's most recorded large mammal. It browses shoots, leaves, nuts and herbs, and heavy browsing can slow tree regrowth.
A ground-dwelling squirrel that eats nuts and seeds and is itself prey for many predators.
A tree squirrel of hardwood forests that eats nuts and seeds such as beechnuts.
A rabbit of forest edges and clearings that eats herbs and is prey for foxes, coyotes and snakes.
A burrowing rodent that eats green plants and is eaten by coyotes, foxes and bears.
A large butterfly whose caterpillars feed on tulip-tree and other hardwood leaves.
An omnivore that eats small mammals, birds, amphibians, fruit and more; GloBI has many prey records.
A big constrictor that eats rodents, rabbits and birds.
A venomous ambush hunter of rocky forest that eats chipmunks, squirrels, rabbits and other small animals.
A small canid that hunts rabbits, rodents and birds. Coyotes may prey on it.
A scavenging bird that cleans up carcasses of deer and other animals and is very well recorded in the area.
Now the main wild predator of deer fawns and small mammals in much of the East, where wolves and cougars have been lost.
An omnivore: mostly plants and nuts such as beechnuts, plus insects, carrion and sometimes deer fawns.
Light reaching the forest floor limits how much understory and wildflowers can grow beneath the canopy.
Leaf litter and rotting wood break down into nutrients that trees and wildflowers take up.

story: New River Gorge in southern West Virginia stretches 53 miles from below Hinton to Hawks Nest State Park. It was established as a national river in 1978 and became a national park and preserve in 2020. It has some of the country's best whitewater rafting and is a popular climbing area.
matters: The 1978 law set out to keep an important stretch of the New River free-flowing. The river begins in North Carolina and flows north into the West Virginia mountains.
